title: No NPCs: Building a Crew of LLM-Powered Characters
author: planetidiot
selftext:
I wanted to see if I could push simulant characters with agency using LLMs as parts of the whole. I started experimenting with no roadmap, no design doc, no grand vision, just the question: Can I build AI-driven characters that remember, evolve, form relationships, and act on their own goals?

The result is an early prototype: [**Journey Space LLM**](https://tippinggoat.itch.io/journey-space-llm)**.**  

You are both the Captain and also the Director of the show. You can talk to your crew as well as reroll AI responses to shape the story, redirect weird answers, or experiment with different models & temperatures.. 

[Captain Chat](https://preview.redd.it/kffnqvlalwne1.png?width=821&format=png&auto=webp&s=c5a017f8b4c4fea1a9c00eaf0a4bd1f3ae35ae67)

Your crew isn’t scripted. They have persistent memories, needs, feelings, and relationships.  Every character is an LLM Simulant, not an NPC. They react dynamically, but also hold grudges, form attachments, and misremember things over time. They think about the past, and it shapes their decisions.

[A Character Remembering the Mission](https://preview.redd.it/68myyqw1lwne1.png?width=546&format=png&auto=webp&s=e0170e078fd042b65910ef015c3edd788ccfae9a)

It’s an experiment in AI-driven emergent storytelling that I've been finding fascinating, messy and... kind of wonderful. If you have an OpenRouter account and don't mind burning some creds on trying it out, [head over to the itch.io and nab the Windows prototype](https://tippinggoat.itch.io/journey-space-llm) (it's free) and *please* share your feedback if this is your cuppa tea. I'd love to hear from other AI game devs, procedural storytellers, or anyone hacking on LLM-driven characters.

[Add additional instructions like the Director of an adlib troupe](https://preview.redd.it/894s6zbflwne1.png?width=865&format=png&auto=webp&s=fe63b665257129805bd81d6e3fbc1eaf7c9d1418)

  
OpenRouter API key and your own credits are required to play.

comments.author: argefox
comments.body:
It's a very interesting concept.

We've been wondering about this for a while as well. Wroking on some kind of 1st person city sim casual game, and the social aspect grows exponential when this comes into play.

Haven't even started working *on it* yet, just my theory, and I assume 2024 had a lot of big games stalled and delayed for this very same reason, Devs are toying with this idea as well. 

Imagine dynamic quests on MMOs, not just grab and fetch. Imagine interesting companions (much like Skyrim did with pure dialogues at first and later via AI API).

I like the proyect, I really have to embrace this potential.

replies.author: planetidiot
replies.body: I went for a "small spaceship" setting just to keep it from getting to insane (not to mention how long it takes for all the API requests). You should definitely start toying with the idea with LLMs. I've had good luck using OpenRouter as you can test many models at once, edit the prompts and retry to try varioius things. You can do a lot to experiment before ever writing code!
